text.p: The price of gold meandered in a narrow range on Monday in a sluggish market lacking clear direction.
Analysts said gold's technical indicators had shed some of their upward momentum and the market was awaiting fresh news before attempting to break out of a price band.
"The range is still $350-$355 and gold should not see enough pressure to put it under $350," an analyst said.
Bullion was fixed at $351.40 per ounce, compared to $352.05 in the morning.
In New York, Comex April gold was also modestly lower, down 60 cents an ounce at $352.40.

Despite the lack of upside impetus, the latest CFTC Commitments of Traders data showed funds had reduced their near-record net short positions in Comex gold sharply. As of March 3 they were only net short 1,213 contracts.
Low short term lease rates, with one-month rates at 0.78 percent on Monday, also confirmed that short positions had fallen away.
Silver was similarly lacklustre and business thin. It was indicated down seven cents from Friday's London close, at $5.23/$5.25 an ounce.
Despite the recent appearance of a bullish "golden cross" of 50- and 200-day on the charts, the metal remained stuck in a $5.20-$5.30 price range.
"Silver has had a problem at $5.30 for some time now," an analyst said.
The other white metals were little changed from morning levels, although some anlaysts said they were vulnerable to futher weakness in the near term.
Platinum was down $2.00 at $379.75/$380.75, while palladium was unchanged at $152.00/$153.00.
There was still no sign of talks beginning between Russia's export negotiators and the Japanese trade houses on 1997 supply contracts.
But news last week that officials in Moscow forecast the first 1997 exports could move by the end of the March had cast a damper on the market, dealers said.
